name: Blue Star Ltd
title: Blue Star Ltd - 500067 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Blue Star's RAC segment margin fell to 2.9% in Q1 as it held share by discounting; management guides Segment II margin above 6.5% for FY27 while cutting pass-through to 5% of an intended 13%.

summary.headline: Blue Star Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT before exceptionals fell 23.7% to Rs125.6 Crore on 13.3% revenue growth, as Segment II EBIT margin dropped to 2.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 13.3% to Rs3,378 Crore, but PBT before exceptional items fell 23.7% to Rs125.6 Crore as commodity costs, rupee depreciation, a late summer and channel inventory squeezed margins. Segment II (Unitary Products) margin fell to 2.9% from 5.8%, as the company chose to defend room AC market share through consumer finance and trade schemes while only partly passing on cost increases. Management guided Segment II FY27 EBIT margin to over 6.5% and called the data-center MEP order book (Rs7,764 Crore total carry-forward order book) the key positive. Net cash rose to Rs900 Crore from Rs371 Crore a year earlier, driven by working capital release.

financial_highlights.change: +13.5% YoY; vs Rs6,923 Crore on 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Segment I - Electro-Mechanical Projects & Commercial AC
segments.commentary: Revenue +15.1% to Rs1,625 Crore with margin of 6.8% (down ~112 bps YoY), hit by commodity and FX costs. Order inflow Rs2,435 Crore (+24%), driven by data centres; commercial office, factory and infrastructure orders were sluggish.

segments.name: Segment II - Unitary Products (RAC, Commercial Refrigeration)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.8% to Rs1,689.3 Crore, margin 2.9% vs 5.8%. Management says Jan-Jun 2026 margin was ~7% when discretionary timing is normalised. Commercial refrigeration degrew ~15%, mainly deep freezers from ice-cream OEMs.

segments.name: Segment III - Professional Electronics & Industrial Systems
segments.commentary: Revenue -9.7% to Rs63.6 Crore, mainly from continued MedTech weakness; segment margin rose to 15.1% from 10.8%.

guidance_outlook: Segment II FY27 EBIT margin guided at over 6.5%; management says it is 'certain' of 6.5% but its aspiration is 7-7.5%, which it does not yet have a view on.
Segment I FY27 margin outlook unchanged at 6.5% to 7%.
Management expects only marginal improvement in Q2 FY27, better Q3 and a 'defining' Q4 once product portfolio rejig is complete; revival expected from late August/September with festive season.

Data-centre MEP: FY27 order inflow guided at ~Rs3,000 Crore and revenue ~Rs1,350-1,400 Crore; FY28 order inflow ~Rs4,500 Crore and revenue ~Rs2,100 Crore; data centre MEP revenue ~Rs4,000 Crore by FY29 (~20% of revenue).
Commercial AC revenue growth of ~10% seen as achievable; 15% not predictable.
Growth-related spend (capex, R&D, digital) of Rs300-350 Crore in FY27 if plan holds; Q1 capex about Rs60-70 Crore.
Export target of additional USD100 million per annum from FY28 over FY26 base; FY26 exports about USD80-85 million.
Management said it remains cautious on FY27 overall.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about Rs60-70 Crore; full-year growth-related spend (capex, R&D intangibles, digital) guided at Rs300-350 Crore.
Data-centre MEP capacity constrained by manpower; company is investing in hiring and specialised professionals and modernising execution, with some infra/building resources diverted to data centres.

Product portfolio rejig under way: cutting some models, outsourcing some portfolio, alternate component sourcing, and redesigns at Sri City and Himachal plants; an alternate/product launch previously planned for six months later is being expedited.
International: product approvals in place with a few customers under CDM route (air-to-air and air-to-water heat pumps); trial orders completed two seasons; scaling awaits US tariff resolution.
Management said manufacturing capacity for RAC industry is about double the market size.
demand_pricing: Management estimates Q1 RAC industry volume grew ~21% and Blue Star ~18% on primary sales; revenue industry ~25% vs Blue Star ~21%. These are management estimates, not audited data.
Tertiary (GFK) RAC market share: lost ~50 bps in April, gained ~10 bps in May and ~50 bps in June; Q1 net loss ~30 bps; Blue Star primary share lost ~65 bps. Year-end share ~14.25%.
Price pass-through: company sought ~13% (cost increase), realised ~5% (3-5% by model); further ~8% needed per management in May.
Trade channel inventory not normalised but 'not alarming'; normal stock estimated at ~60 days overall or ~45 days for trade alone. Energy label change led the trade to over-stock old-label products.
Commercial refrigeration demand muted (deep freezers, ice-cream OEMs, cold rooms, QSR); management says market share held.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Segment II margin drop, what was the impact of deferred discretionary costs, and what other levers exist to restore margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no deferred cost carried from Q4 into Q1; the Q1 margin reflects actual costs. The shortfall came from only partly passing on input costs and from consumer finance, trade schemes and in-shop promotions to defend tertiary share. Levers are product portfolio rejig, alternate components, outsourcing and redesigns, with Q2 seen as marginal improvement, Q3 better and Q4 the defining quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MEP revenue guidance being upgraded from the earlier 8-10% growth view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commercial AC MEP growth of 8-10% still holds but could reach about 12% for a couple of years because of data-centre demand. Data-centre FY27 order inflow is guided at about Rs3,000 Crore and revenue at about Rs1,350 Crore, with FY28 at about Rs4,500 Crore orders and Rs2,100 Crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q2 pressures from imported compressors and copper, and could the 6.5% Segment II margin guidance taper further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said input costs will stay higher in Q2 and expects only marginal improvement, with no negative territory expected. It is certain of 6.5% for FY27 and said 7-7.5% is an aspiration, not yet confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What were the trade schemes and was the discounting competition-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described costs for consumer finance, in-shop demonstrators, advertising and field marketing incurred in May and June to help dealers liquidate. It said many competitors held lower prices and some brands sold older-price stock into June, and that Blue Star chose share defence over margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is channel inventory normalised, and what price increase is still needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory is not normalised but not alarming; normal stock is about 60 days overall or about 45 days for trade. Management said about 8% more price was needed in May, and it does not expect the market to accept the full amount.

qa_highlights.question: Was the commercial refrigeration degrowth a market share loss or industry demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market share was held and the ~15% degrowth in deep freezers reflects muted industry demand from ice-cream OEMs and rate-contract buyers, not share loss.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 volume and value growth estimates for RAC, and the market share and primary sales figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated RAC industry volume up ~21% vs Blue Star ~18%, and revenue up ~25% vs Blue Star ~21%, on a primary basis. Tertiary share fell ~30 bps in Q1 and primary share fell ~65 bps; year-end share is expected at ~14.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export run-rate and the FY28 export target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 exports were about USD80-85 million, versus about USD55-60 million the year before. The target is an additional USD100 million per annum from FY28 over the FY26 base, with US volumes dependent on tariff resolution.

risks_watch: Segment II margin recovery depends on the product portfolio rejig and cost take-out; management guides marginal improvement in Q2 and a defining Q4, so Q2 and Q3 margins are the next checkpoints.

Continued input cost pressure: copper at record levels, rupee volatility, petroleum-linked costs, and about 40% of BOM imported (compressors), with only about 5% of a ~13% cost increase passed on so far.

Market share versus margin trade-off: tertiary share down ~30 bps in Q1, year-end share guided to ~14.25%, and competition from OEM-manufactured entry-level brands and excess industry capacity (~double market size).
Channel inventory above normal (~60 days overall, ~45 days trade) could delay primary sales until festive-season restocking from late August/September.
Data-centre MEP execution is constrained by manpower and diverted infra/building resources; the business is described as cyclical, with a possible dip after the current rush.
Commercial refrigeration (deep freezers, cold rooms) degrew ~15%; festive-season revival is expected but not yet visible. Export ramp-up depends on US tariff resolution.
key_quotes: Broadly, we have fallen short of the expectations, but the fundamentals are strong.
We took a hit in the operating margin in order to more or less maintain our market share, still the, the commodity prices are going up.
As of now, we have a visibility to close the year with an operating margin of over 6.5% for segment II in financial year FY27.
I am certain we will. Unless something completely untoward happens, a full-blown war in the Middle East and the global economy collapses.
summary.management_tone: Candid and defensive on Segment II: management admits the margin miss and fallen-short expectations but stays confident on recovery to over 6.5% for FY27, while declining to commit to 7-7.5%. It is more confident on data-centre MEP and the net cash position, and cautious overall on FY27, with Q2 flagged as a lean quarter.

adds.what: Data-centre MEP delivery capacity: manpower hiring and modernised execution (not a plant; capacity constrained by manpower)
International CDM-route heat pump scaling (air-to-air and air-to-water), awaiting US tariff resolution

growth.why: Management guides Segment II FY27 EBIT margin above 6.5% (described as 'certain') and Segment I margin at 6.5-7%, with data-centre MEP order inflow ~Rs3,000 Crore and revenue ~Rs1,350-1,400 Crore backed by a Rs7,764 Crore carry-forward order book; commercial AC growth of ~10% seen as achievable, but management remains cautious on FY27 overall and price pass-through is only ~5% against ~13% sought.
